lines.text: Two points on a number line. Then a chase begins.
lines.caption: Two points on a number line. Then a chase begins.

lines.text: Each new point lands halfway between the last two. <short pause> Where does it end up?
lines.caption: Each new point lands halfway between the last two. Where does it end up?

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's follow the chase together.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's follow the chase together.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Point P one is at zero, and point P two is at sixty-four, on a number line.
lines.caption: Point P one is at zero, and point P two is at sixty-four, on a number line.

lines.text: Each later point is the midpoint of the two points before it.
lines.caption: Each later point is the midpoint of the two points before it.

lines.text: So P three is at thirty-two, and P four is at forty-eight.
lines.caption: So P three is at thirty-two, and P four is at forty-eight.

lines.text: Where does P ten land?
lines.caption: Where does P ten land?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we really know?
lines.caption: So what do we really know?

lines.text: We start with two points. Each new point is the midpoint of the newest two.
lines.caption: We start with two points. Each new point is the midpoint of the newest two.

lines.text: We need P ten. That's eight more midpoints after P two.
lines.caption: We need P ten. That's eight more midpoints after P two.

lines.text: The choices use decimals. Here's a key for halves, quarters and eighths.
lines.caption: The choices use decimals. Here's a key for halves, quarters and eighths.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Let's make a list, one point at a time, and watch the jumps.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Let's make a list, one point at a time, and watch the jumps.

lines.text: From zero to sixty-four is a jump of sixty-four, to the right.
lines.caption: From zero to sixty-four is a jump of sixty-four, to the right.

lines.text: P three is the midpoint, thirty-two. That's a jump of thirty-two, back to the left.
lines.caption: P three is the midpoint, thirty-two. That's a jump of thirty-two, back to the left.

lines.text: P four is halfway between thirty-two and sixty-four. That's forty-eight, sixteen to the right.
lines.caption: P four is halfway between thirty-two and sixty-four. That's forty-eight, sixteen to the right.

lines.text: Notice the pattern? Each jump is half the one before, and it flips direction.
lines.caption: Notice the pattern? Each jump is half the one before, and it flips direction.

lines.text: Why? The new point sits halfway along the last jump. So it goes back, half as far.
lines.caption: Why? The new point sits halfway along the last jump. So it goes back, half as far.

lines.text: So the next jumps are eight left, four right, two left, and one right.
lines.caption: So the next jumps are eight left, four right, two left, and one right.

lines.text: That puts P five at forty, P six at forty-four, P seven at forty-two, and P eight at forty-three.
lines.caption: That puts P five at forty, P six at forty-four, P seven at forty-two, and P eight at forty-three.

lines.text: See how the points squeeze closer and closer? They close in on one spot.
lines.caption: See how the points squeeze closer and closer? They close in on one spot.

lines.text: Next, a jump of one half to the left. P nine is forty-two and a half.
lines.caption: Next, a jump of one half to the left. P nine is forty-two and a half.

lines.text: Last, a jump of one quarter to the right.
lines.caption: Last, a jump of one quarter to the right.

lines.text: P ten is forty-two and three quarters! <short pause> The answer is C.
lines.caption: P ten is forty-two and three quarters! The answer is C.

lines.text: Here's a clever second way. Start at zero, and add up all nine jumps.
lines.caption: Here's a clever second way. Start at zero, and add up all nine jumps.

lines.text: Right jumps are plus, left jumps are minus. Sixty-four, minus thirty-two, plus sixteen, and so on.
lines.caption: Right jumps are plus, left jumps are minus. Sixty-four, minus thirty-two, plus sixteen, and so on.

lines.text: Let's pair them up. Sixty-four minus thirty-two is thirty-two.
lines.caption: Let's pair them up. Sixty-four minus thirty-two is thirty-two.

lines.text: Sixteen minus eight is eight. Four minus two is two.
lines.caption: Sixteen minus eight is eight. Four minus two is two.

lines.text: One minus one half is one half. The last jump, one quarter, is on its own.
lines.caption: One minus one half is one half. The last jump, one quarter, is on its own.

lines.text: Look, each pair is a quarter of the pair before: thirty-two, eight, two, one half.
lines.caption: Look, each pair is a quarter of the pair before: thirty-two, eight, two, one half.

lines.text: Thirty-two plus eight plus two is forty-two.
lines.caption: Thirty-two plus eight plus two is forty-two.

lines.text: One half plus one quarter is three quarters. So it's forty-two and three quarters again!
lines.caption: One half plus one quarter is three quarters. So it's forty-two and three quarters again!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When there are lots of steps, pairs keep it tidy.
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When there are lots of steps, pairs keep it tidy.

lines.text: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a real point in the chase!
lines.caption: Now, let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a real point in the chase!

lines.text: Forty-two and a half is P nine. That answer is one step early.
lines.caption: Forty-two and a half is P nine. That answer is one step early.

lines.text: Forty-three is P eight. You'd get it if you stopped before the jumps turned into fractions.
lines.caption: Forty-three is P eight. You'd get it if you stopped before the jumps turned into fractions.

lines.text: Forty-four is P six. That stops far too early.
lines.caption: Forty-four is P six. That stops far too early.

lines.text: Next, forty-two and five over eight. That is P eleven, one step late.
lines.caption: Next, forty-two and five over eight. That is P eleven, one step late.

lines.text: You'd get it if you called the first point P zero. Then your tenth point is really P eleven.
lines.caption: You'd get it if you called the first point P zero. Then your tenth point is really P eleven.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. Write the point number next to every point as you go.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. Write the point number next to every point as you go.

lines.text: Ready for a challenge? Here's a new chase.
lines.caption: Ready for a challenge? Here's a new chase.

lines.text: P one is at zero again, but P two is at thirty-two.
lines.caption: P one is at zero again, but P two is at thirty-two.

lines.text: Each point is the midpoint of the two before it. Where is P nine?
lines.caption: Each point is the midpoint of the two before it. Where is P nine?

lines.text: Pause the video, and go for it!
lines.caption: Pause the video, and go for it!

lines.text: Let's check. The jumps start at thirty-two, then halve and flip each time.
lines.caption: Let's check. The jumps start at thirty-two, then halve and flip each time.

lines.text: Thirty-two right, sixteen left, eight right, four left, two right, one left.
lines.caption: Thirty-two right, sixteen left, eight right, four left, two right, one left.

lines.text: Then a half to the right, and a quarter to the left. That's eight jumps, which takes us to P nine.
lines.caption: Then a half to the right, and a quarter to the left. That's eight jumps, which takes us to P nine.

lines.text: Pair them up. Thirty-two minus sixteen is sixteen. Eight minus four is four.
lines.caption: Pair them up. Thirty-two minus sixteen is sixteen. Eight minus four is four.

lines.text: Two minus one is one. One half minus one quarter is one quarter.
lines.caption: Two minus one is one. One half minus one quarter is one quarter.

lines.text: Sixteen plus four plus one is twenty-one. Then add one quarter.
lines.caption: Sixteen plus four plus one is twenty-one. Then add one quarter.

lines.text: So P nine is twenty-one and a quarter! If you found that, amazing work!
lines.caption: So P nine is twenty-one and a quarter! If you found that, amazing work!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: When each new point is a midpoint, each new jump is half the one before, and flips direction.
lines.caption: When each new point is a midpoint, each new jump is half the one before, and flips direction.

lines.text: So list the points one at a time, and watch the jumps. The points close in on one value.
lines.caption: So list the points one at a time, and watch the jumps. The points close in on one value.

lines.text: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
lines.caption: I'm Vantee. Keep exploring, and I'll see you next time!
